newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Patience needed in S.African oil industry change.
newsitem.headline: Patience needed in S.African oil industry change.

text.p: South African Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna on Wednesday called for patience in the oil industry as his department mulled over new policy options.
"We know this matter is urgent. Rest assured, the complex and far-reaching issue of de- or re-regulation is being addressed," Maduna said as he introduced his 1997/98 budget in parliament.

He said he was aware that players in the industry had to be assured about the new "rules of the game" because they had to make pressing investment decisions about expanding South Africa's crude oil refining capacity.
"Currently refining capacity has reached capacity and within the next five years additional facilities will be required," Maduna said.
Imports would supplement demand until a major new refinery became economically viable.
Maduna was appointed in July to take over from the National Party's Pik Botha when the NP left the government of national unity.
Asked if he planned to dismantle the companies currently dominating the oil industry, he said this was not part of his brief.
"I can't dismantle them until our own competition laws address the lack of competition," he said.
"There can't be competition if there have been suggestions that there is collusion of all sorts."
